families.summary: EchoConfidence is software-as-a-medical-device that classifies transthoracic echo views, segments cardiac chambers and great vessels, and produces automated structural, functional and Doppler measurements (the company states over 100 measurements) with editable contours and report generation. FDA 510(k) K250670 (cleared 2025-06-30) was supported by a 200-patient retrospective US core-lab study comparing AI mean absolute error against three expert readers, using the +25% upper-95%-CI criterion borrowed from the us2.ai predicate.
families.intended_use_quote: EchoConfidence is Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) that displays images from a Transthoracic Echocardiogram, and assists the user in reviewing the images, making measurements and writing a report.
families.indications_for_use_quote: EchoConfidence is Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) that displays images from a Transthoracic Echocardiogram, and assists the user in reviewing the images, making measurements and writing a report. The intended medical indication is for patients requiring review or analysis of their echocardiographic images acquired for their cardiac anatomy, structure and function. This includes automatic view classification; segmentation of cardiac structures including the left and right ventricle, chamber walls, left and right atria and great vessels; measures of cardiac function; and Doppler assessments. The intended patient population is both healthy individuals and patients in whom an underlying cardiac disease is known or suspected; the intended patient age range is for adults (>= 22 years old) and adolescent in the age range 18 – 21 years old.
embedded_ai_features: automatic view classification (company states 23 view classes)
segmentation of LV, RV, chamber walls, LA, RA and great vessels
automated measures of cardiac function
Doppler assessments
manual editing of AI contours/fiducial points (human-in-the-loop)
multi-beat averaging (company)
batch analysis and serial-scan comparison (company)

performance_claims.endpoint: Primary endpoint: AI mean absolute error vs 3 human experts compared with inter-expert MAE, across all measurements (over 100), per case
performance_claims.metric: Median difference between AI-vs-expert MAE and expert-vs-expert MAE, expressed as % of expert MAE; acceptance = upper 95% bootstrap CI < +25%
performance_claims.value: Acceptance criterion (upper 95% bootstrap CI of the AI-minus-expert MAE difference < +25% of expert MAE) reported as met. Point estimate 'substantially below 0%' in the majority of cases; the statement that the upper 95% CI is '<0%' appears in the subgroup-reporting sentence. No numeric point estimates or CIs are given in the summary.
performance_claims.comparator: 3 US-accredited, US-based core-lab expert readers measuring independently; ~10% of measurements reviewed/adjusted by a physician
performance_claims.dataset_description: 200 comprehensive echocardiograms from 200 different patients delivered via a US Echocardiography CoreLab; non-public data; core lab did not supply any training data
performance_claims.subgroup_notes: Primary analysis repeated in 20 subgroups (age, gender, ethnicity, cardiac pathologies, ultrasound vendor/model, year of scan, qualitative image quality); finding stated to be consistent across subgroups with wider CIs; subgroup tables are in the IFU, not the summary; subgroup analyses are described but no subgroup numbers appear in the summary
performance_claims.quote: The primary criteria for acceptance are that the upper 95% confidence interval is less than +25%. In the majority of cases the point estimate is substantially below 0% (i.e. the AI agrees with the humans more than they agree with each other. [...] The reporting shows that the point estimation is such that the AI agrees with the human experts better than the humans agree with themselves: that the upper 95% confidence interval is also <0%, and well below the +25% criterion standard; across the subgroups, whilst there is increased noise and wider confidence intervals (as would be expected with fewer cases), the finding is consistent amongst the subgroups.

performance_claims.endpoint: Agreement of AI measurements with average of expert measurements
performance_claims.value: Reported to FDA; numeric values not provided in the 510(k) summary
performance_claims.comparator: Average of the 3 human experts' measurements
performance_claims.quote: Bland-Altman analysis was reported, based on averages of the human experts’ measurements.

training_data.description: Company newsletter dated 'JULY, 2025' (PDF, verified 2026-09-05): 'Trained on 100,000+ echo images from over 20,000 patients'; company product page: 'fixed Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) trained on over 100,000 images'. FDA summary states only that the development/internal-test dataset came from a separate (non-core-lab) source, with patients tagged as training or internal testing; no size given in the FDA summary. Figures are unaudited company claims.

validation_data.description: 200 comprehensive TTE studies from 200 patients from a US Echocardiography CoreLab (non-public data held on core-lab servers); 3 US-based expert readers; demographic/subgroup breakdown (age, gender, ethnicity, pathology, vendor/model, scan year, image quality) tabulated in the IFU

prior_validations.description: Company states EchoConfidence was 'Validated against six international expert readers', 'Benchmarked using Mean Absolute Error (MAE) to match inter-expert consistency' and 'Reviewed using unseen datasets labelled by 8–15 certified cardiologists and sonographers' (no numbers or publication cited).
Company product page claims 'over 95% accuracy across 23 automatic view classifications' and 'Automated AI measurement of >98% of echo parameters'; CE Class IIb marked.

open_questions: No peer-reviewed publication describing EchoConfidence or its validation was found on PubMed (searches: 'EchoConfidence', 'Mycardium[Affiliation]'); the whitepapers listed on the company page (Francis/Shun-Shin/Stowell collaborative-AI work; Howard et al. video classification) are not explicitly attributed to the product, so they were not catalogued.
Numeric point estimates and CIs for the primary MAE endpoint, and Bland-Altman bias/LoA, are not in the 510(k) summary (subgroup tables are said to be in the IFU).
The 510(k) summary's Device Description field (page 5) did not survive text extraction; the device description here relies on the IFU and company materials.
Training set size (100,000+ images / >20,000 patients) is a company claim only; the FDA summary gives no numbers.
The 18-21 year adolescent subgroup was explicitly not evaluated separately (summary p.6).
Company claim of 'over 40% improvement in measurement precision' (newsletter) has no cited source.
Deployment model (cloud vs on-premise) is not stated in the FDA summary; company says vendor-neutral with PACS/EHR integration.

Company-sourced figures (100,000+ images, 20,000 patients, six international readers, 8-15 labellers, '>95% accuracy across 23 automatic view classifications', '>98% of echo parameters', 'over 40% improvement in measurement precision') were confirmed to appear on the cited company pages on 2026-09-05 but have no independent or FDA corroboration.

Verification 2026-09-05: PubMed searches 'EchoConfidence' (0 hits), 'Mycardium AND echocardiography' (24 hits, none about the product; 'Mycardium' matches misspellings of myocardium) and 'Mycardium[Affiliation]' (2 unrelated MRA papers); Europe PMC full-text search for 'EchoConfidence' returned 1 unrelated hit. No product paper exists to add.

families.summary: Clarius Ejection Fraction AI is a deep-learning segmentation/landmark algorithm embedded in the Clarius App that automatically selects end-diastolic and end-systolic frames and computes LVEF in real time from PLAX (Teichholz), PSAX (fractional area change) and apical 4-/2-chamber (single-plane Simpson) views acquired with Clarius PA HD3, PAL HD3 and C3 HD3 handheld scanners. K253593 (cleared 2026-03-02, with a PCCP) was supported by a 279-exam retrospective non-inferiority study against three blinded reviewers.
families.intended_use_quote: Intended for use as an assistive tool utilizing an artificial intelligence/machine learning-based algorithm for semi-automated measurement of cardiac ultrasound images for determination of left ventricular ejection fraction.
families.indications_for_use_quote: Clarius Ejection Fraction AI is intended for semi- automatic non -invasive measurement of the left ventricular ejection fraction on ultrasound data acquired by the Clarius Ultrasound Scanner (i.e., phased array and curvilinear scanners). The user shall be a healthcare professional trained and qualified in ultrasound. The user retains the responsibility of confirming the validity of the measurements based on standard practices and clinical judgment. Clarius Ejection Fraction Al is intended for use in adult patients only.
embedded_ai_features: automatic capture of ED and ES frames
deep-learning LV segmentation mask or landmark markers in ED and ES
automatic LVEF calculation (single-plane Simpson for apical, fractional area change for PSAX, Teichholz for PLAX)
manual caliper adjustment of AI result
real-time display in Clarius App during scanning (Cardiac Basic / Cardiac Advanced presets)

notable_flags: not stand-alone software (integrated into Clarius App)

performance_claims.quote: The automatic LV EF measurement was found to be non-inferior to that of experienced ultrasound users as shown by statistically significant p-values of 5.57e-21 (97.5%CI: - inf, -3.00), 1.57e-36 (97.5%CI: - inf, -2.1) and 1.12e -18 (97.5%CI: - inf, -2.38) for the Apical, PSAX and PLAX views respectively.

training_data.description: FDA summary: model developed with training, tuning (validation) and internal-testing sets collected from the Clarius Cloud and/or partner clinics, partitioned by unique anonymous patient identifier; institutions used for development were excluded from the verification study. No sizes given. Company press release: 'developed using thousands of cardiac ultrasound images annotated by clinicians'.

prior_validations.description: A clinical design-validation (usability) study with production-equivalent units in a simulated use environment showed users could activate the tool on C3 HD3 / PA HD3, obtain PLAX/PSAX/apical EF, view ED/ES frames and adjust results; no quantitative results reported.

open_questions: No peer-reviewed publication of Clarius Ejection Fraction AI was found on PubMed (searches for 'Clarius' with ejection fraction / deep learning / affiliation).
Number of unique patients and number of contributing sites in the 279-exam verification set are not stated (counts are per exam/image, and 21 exams have unknown origin).
Bias / limits of agreement and per-scanner (C3 HD3 vs PA HD3) ICCs are not reported in the summary.
Training/tuning/internal-test set sizes are not disclosed; company says only 'thousands of images'.
Clarius press release announcing clearance is dated June 2, 2026, three months after the FDA decision date (2026-03-02).
PCCP scope (new scanners, hyperparameters, post-processing, masked-autoencoder architecture) means the marketed model may change without a new 510(k).

Verification 2026-09-05: PubMed 'Clarius AND ejection fraction' (2 hits: a leadless-pacemaker trial and a UBC CycleGAN image-translation paper that used Clarius scanners), 'Clarius AND echocardiography' (3 hits, EFSUMB guidelines and the CycleGAN paper), 'Clarius[Affiliation] AND cardiac' (3 Jefferson SHAPE microbubble papers); Europe PMC full-text search 'Clarius AND ejection fraction' (23 hits, none evaluating Clarius Ejection Fraction AI). No product paper exists to add.

Company press-release wording ('developed using thousands of cardiac ultrasound images annotated by clinicians', availability on 'PA, PAL and C3 HD3', dateline 'June 02, 2026') confirmed on the cited page on 2026-09-05.

families.summary: Ligence Heart is fully automated post-processing software that classifies 2D TTE views, selects cardiac cycles, detects borders and generates a PACS-compatible structured report that the clinician can accept or edit. K252105 (2025-09-26) covered four LV measurements (biplane LVEF, LVEDV, LVESV and lateral e') validated on 524 analysable studies at a US core lab using the individual equivalence coefficient; K253535 (2026-02-27, 510(k) statement only) added fully automated LV global longitudinal and segmental strain according to the company.
families.indications_for_use_quote: Ligence Heart is a fully automated software platform that processes, analyses and makes measurements on acquired transthoracic cardiac ultrasound images, automatically producing a full report with measurements of several key cardiac structural and functional parameters. The data produced by this software is intended to be used to support qualified cardiologists or sonographers for clinical decision making. Ligence Heart is indicated for use in adult patients. Ligence Heart has not been validated for the assessment of congenital heart disease, valve disease, pericardial disease, and/or intra-cardiac lesions (e.g., tumors, thrombi). Limitations: * Poor image capture will lead to poor annotations and subsequent measurements. * Multiple image quality algorithms are used to filter out images of poor quality. * Our software complements good patient care and does not exempt the user from the responsibility to provide supervision, clinically review the patient, and make appropriate clinical decisions. * If no gender is present, female referenced guideline values will be used for conclusions. * If Body Surface Area (BSA) is not present, indexed values cannot be provided. * During image acquisition, inappropriate use of the echo machine, use of non-cardiac ultrasound probes, or use of suboptimal settings (e.g., gain, contrast, depth) may lead to lower accuracy of the software. * Ligence Heart has not been validated in patients with prosthetic or surgically altered cardiac valves, implantable intracardiac devices, or irregular (non-sinus) rhythm; these conditions may affect automated measurement accuracy.
embedded_ai_features: machine-learning view classification
automatic cardiac cycle (clip) selection
automatic endocardial border detection
biplane method-of-disks LVEF, LVEDV, LVESV
lateral mitral annular e' (tissue Doppler)
image-quality filtering algorithms
automated structured report with guideline reference ranges, user accept/edit, PDF export
fully automated LV global longitudinal strain and segmental strain (added with K253535, per company)

clearances.changes_summary: FDA posted a 510(k) Statement rather than a Summary, so predicates, changes and performance data are not public. The FDA PDF does contain an image-only Indications for Use form (page 4) whose wording is identical to the K252105 IFU (fully automated measurement/reporting on adult TTE; same exclusions and limitations; Prescription Use) and does not mention strain. The company announcement (2026-04-14) states this second clearance covers Ligence Heart v4.0.0 and adds fully automated LV global longitudinal strain and segmental strain with an interactive Strain View UI plus private-cloud deployment.
notable_flags: IFU text identical to K252105 (image-only page)

performance_claims.endpoint: Interchangeability of automated LVEF, LVEDV, LVESV (biplane MOD) and lateral e' with expert sonographer measurements
performance_claims.metric: Reference-scaled Individual Equivalence Coefficient (IEC); non-inferiority if upper 95% CI < 0.25
performance_claims.value: All four parameters met the criterion (upper 95% CI of IEC < 0.25); point estimates not reported
performance_claims.comparator: Three independent expert sonographers at a US independent echocardiography core laboratory
performance_claims.dataset_description: 600 previously acquired echocardiograms at a US core lab; 76 excluded for missing views or corrupt metadata; 524 analysed by all three readers. Age 49.48 ± 13.56 y; male 319 (60.88%), female 205 (39.12%); height 173.36 ± 10.52 cm; weight 88.92 ± 21.11 kg; LVEF 34.45 ± 15.78%
performance_claims.subgroup_notes: LVEF distribution: normal >50% 120 (22.90%), reduced <50% 404 (77.10%) of which mildly reduced 40-50% 64 (12.21%), moderately reduced 30-40% 85 (16.22%), severely reduced <30% 255 (48.66%). No sex/vendor/image-quality subgroup results reported.
performance_claims.quote: Primary Clinical Performance Endpoint was Individual Equivalence Coefficient (IEC). Agreement between Ligence Heart and three independent expert sonographers was quantified using the reference-scaled IEC. Automated measurements are deemed interchangeable when the upper level of the IEC 95% confidence interval was < 0.25, a non-inferiority margin derived from individual-bioequivalence principles. All four parameters met the non-inferiority criterion, confirming that Ligence Heart measurements are interchangeable with expert human measurements.

performance_claims.endpoint: Agreement of automated LVEF, LVEDV, LVESV and lateral e' with expert measurements (secondary)
performance_claims.value: ICC >= 0.90 for all four parameters (per-parameter values not given)
performance_claims.comparator: Three independent expert sonographers (US core lab)
performance_claims.quote: Secondary agreement metrics were consistent with the IEC result. Intraclass Correlation Coefficients (ICC) were ≥ 0.90 for all four parameters. No device-related adverse events, malfunctions, or unmediated issues occurred during the study.

performance_claims.value: 76 of 600 studies excluded (missing views or corrupt metadata); 524 analysed
performance_claims.dataset_description: 600 previously acquired echocardiograms at a US independent echocardiography core laboratory
performance_claims.quote: A formal retrospective non-interventional validation study was conducted at a U.S. based independent Echocardiography Core Laboratory using 600 previously acquired echocardiograms to evaluate the performance of the device for each claimed measurement. Test datasets were strictly segregated from algorithm training datasets, as they are from completely separate cohorts. A cumulative total of 76 studies were excluded because of missing views or corrupt metadata. Ultimately, 524 echocardiographic studies were assessed by all three human readers, satisfied the predefined quality criteria, and were included in the final analysis.

training_data.description: FDA summary states only that test datasets were 'strictly segregated from algorithm training datasets, as they are from completely separate cohorts'; no training set size, sites or vendors given. No company source with training-set numbers was found.

validation_data.description: 600 previously acquired TTE studies at a US independent echocardiography core lab, 524 analysable; mean age 49.5 y, 61% male, mean LVEF 34.5% with 77% having LVEF <50%; three expert sonographer readers

prior_validations.description: CE mark under MDR 2017/745 as a Class IIa device (company news).

Company reports an ESC-presented Dresden study (Botan et al.) of 1,245 patients in which fully automated aortic-valve/aortic-stenosis parameters correlated with clinician values (R ~0.81-0.98); no PubMed record located.
Company reports Ligence Heart validated against CMR-referenced LVEF at John Paul II Hospital, Krakow (Polish Archives of Internal Medicine 2025; R = 0.87 vs CMR, R = 0.88-0.90 vs experts).

papers.title: Artificial intelligence for automated evaluation of aortic measurements in 2D echocardiography: Feasibility, accuracy, and reproducibility
papers.key_result: Company-authored. Ligence Heart v2 PLAX aortic measurements (annulus, sinus, STJ, ascending aorta) feasible in 93-95% of 58 studies; automated values correlated more strongly with an expert cardiologist than a group of three cardiologists did.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Driven Automated Assessment of Left Ventricular Diastolic Function in Echocardiography
papers.key_result: Company-authored prospective study; Ligence Heart diastolic parameters vs expert manual: E velocity r = 0.93, A velocity r = 0.88, E/A r = 0.94, LAVi r = 0.92; lower agreement for TR velocity; good classification of normal and severe diastolic dysfunction, more variability in intermediate grades.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence implementation in automated heart chambers quantification during pharmacological stress echocardiography
papers.key_result: Company-authored multi-centre study (5 sites, 4 countries) of pharmacological stress echo: ML LV and LA volumes vs expert tracings ICC 0.84-0.93 at rest and stress; moderate agreement for RA/RV areas; poor image quality reduced yield.

papers.title: Left ventricular ejection fraction assessment: artificial intelligence compared with echocardiography expert and cardiac magnetic resonance measurements
papers.key_result: Independent (Krakow) retrospective study; AI multiloop LVEF vs CMR R = 0.87 (kappa 0.68) and vs experts R = 0.88-0.90; single best-loop AI vs CMR R = 0.89 (kappa 0.75). Attribution to Ligence Heart is from the vendor's news page; the PubMed abstract does not name the product.

papers.title: Fully Automatic AI-Based Quantification of LV Mass in Echocardiography: A Multimodality Validation
papers.key_result: Dresden study of 218 patients vs CT reference: AI LV mass hybrid method ICC 0.76 / MAPE 0.16 (linear method ICC 0.49 / MAPE 0.44); AI reduced measurement error ~20% vs experts and reclassified 34% of RWT+ cases; AUC for increased LV mass 0.78 vs 0.71 (linear) and 0.84 vs 0.77 (hybrid); test-retest CV 7.8% and 8.1% (n = 40). Numbers verified against the PubMed abstract. Attribution to Ligence Heart is from the vendor's news page; the abstract does not name the product.

papers.title: Validation of a fully automated AI system for accurate left ventricular mass measurement in echocardiography
papers.journal: European Heart Journal - Cardiovascular Imaging (abstract supplement)
papers.key_result: Congress abstract (Dresden; EHJ-CVI 26 Suppl 1, 2025): final cohort 164 patients (101 AS, 48 MR, 41 TR) with same-day echo and CT; AI vs human LV mass r = 0.83, MAE 22 g; AI vs CT r = 0.69, MAE 28 g versus human vs CT r = 0.62, MAE 37 g; feasibility AI 91%, human 95%, CT 99%. Numbers verified in the Crossref abstract; attribution to Ligence Heart comes from the vendor's news page (the abstract does not name the product).

papers.title: Model-guided medicine for early diagnosis of transthyretin-associated cardiac amyloidosis using multimodal data integration and standardized interoperable models (the CRONOS-ATTR study)
papers.journal: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery
papers.key_result: Uses Ligence Heart echo outputs (with Cardiolyse ECG AI) as inputs to an XGBoost ATTR-CM screening model (AUC 0.84); not a validation of Ligence Heart measurements.

papers.title: Exploring the Potential of Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Echocardiography-Preliminary Results from the First Pediatric Study Using AI Software Developed for Adults
papers.key_result: Independent (Bordeaux) pediatric study outside the cleared adult indication: Ligence Heart (named in the PMC full text) analysed 2D TTE from 45 children (mean age 8.2 +/- 5.7 y) with normal or near-normal hearts; 23 features compared with a junior and a senior physician. Bland-Altman agreement with the senior physician was good for aortic annulus and E wave at all ages, and for STJ and EF only in children older than 9 years; other features showed poor agreement.

open_questions: K253535 was filed with a 510(k) Statement, so its predicates, changes and performance data are not public. Its IFU is public (image-only page 4 of the FDA PDF) and is word-for-word the K252105 IFU, with no mention of strain; the GLS/strain content of that clearance therefore rests solely on the company's 2026-04-14 announcement.
Per-parameter IEC point estimates/CIs and per-parameter ICCs for K252105 are not given (only 'all met <0.25' and 'ICC >= 0.90').
Training data size, sites and vendors are not disclosed in either FDA document or on the company site.
The K252105 validation cohort is heavily enriched for reduced LVEF (77% <50%; 49% <30%) and its vendor/image-quality mix is not described.

Dresden-group papers on fully automated LVEF (Sveric 2023 Diagnostics PMID 37046515; Sveric 2024 Int J Cardiol PMID 37757986) and GLS (Sveric 2024 EHJ Imaging Methods and Practice PMID 39712903) likely evaluate Ligence Heart, but the PMC full texts of 37046515 and 39712903 (checked 2026-09-05) and the abstract of 37757986 do not name the vendor, so they were not catalogued.
Company FDA-clearance news page is dated 2025-11-26, two months after the 2025-09-26 decision date.
FDA summary p.9 contains a garbled sentence ('No distinctions between the two systems do not introduce new questions').

Jiang et al. 2023 (Frontiers Cardiovasc Med, PMID 38045908) is tabulated as 'Ligence Heart (version 2)' in a 2026 meta-analysis (Roberts et al., EHJ Digital Health, PMID 41853635), but its own methods state the AI platform was Ultromics EchoGo Core (Ligence appears only in a conflict-of-interest statement), so it was not catalogued.

Verification 2026-09-05: PubMed 'Ligence Heart' (7 hits), 'Ligence AND echocardiography' (6), 'Ligence[Affiliation]' (5) and Europe PMC full-text '"Ligence Heart"' (9) yielded one additional product-specific paper (Vasile 2023, pediatric), now added; remaining hits were the already-listed papers, reviews, an EVOLVED-trial post hoc analysis, an EchoGo Pro study and the Stress Echo 2030 protocol.

notes: All four FDA documents were read in full. K250670 (EchoConfidence) and K252105 (Ligence Heart) are terse summaries that report acceptance-criterion outcomes without point estimates; K253593 (Clarius) is the only one with tabulated statistics and it carries a PCCP; K253535 (Ligence Heart second clearance) is a 510(k) Statement with no public summary. ClinicalTrials.gov searches for 'Ligence', 'Mycardium', 'EchoConfidence' and 'Clarius ejection fraction' returned no studies. No peer-reviewed papers were found for EchoConfidence or Clarius EF AI; Ligence has company-authored feasibility papers and independent Krakow/Dresden validations (product attribution for the latter comes from the vendor's site). Company-sourced numbers (Mycardium 100,000+ images / 20,000 patients; Clarius 'thousands of images') are labelled as such. Page numbers refer to the '===== PAGE n =====' markers in the extracted text files. VERIFICATION PASS (2026-09-05): all quotes located in the cited FDA text files at the cited pages; decision dates, product codes and applicants match openFDA; predicates K210791/K191171 (K250670), K210747 (K253593) and K210791 (K252105) appear in the summaries; PCCP appears only in K253593. K253535 page 4 (image-only) was rendered from the PDF and is an IFU form identical to the K252105 IFU. All seven Ligence DOIs resolved via Crossref and PMIDs via PubMed efetch; one additional product-specific paper (Vasile 2023) was added; a meta-analysis (PMID 41853635) that lists Ligence Heart among included tools was not added because it is not about this product. Company-page claims were re-fetched and confirmed to appear as quoted but remain uncorroborated. Local file paths were replaced with public FDA URLs.
